summary.intent: Get ADR 0026 (making the type checker, via tsrs, the authority for prop types with oxc supplying candidates/defaults/locations) drafted by a subagent, pushed, and turned into a PR with a filled body for the user to review.
summary.outcome: The subagent wrote ADR 0026 (Proposed, commit f35f10c9, signed) and pushed it to a branch; PR #386 was opened with title and body, CI had just started, and the ADR is kept as Proposed pending the user's decision and spike re-confirmation of unverified claims.

repo: ADRs live in docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md, are indexed in docs/adr/README.md, and use a Status line with a comma convention for supersession (e.g. ', superseded in part by 0026 (proposed)' on 0006 and 0007).
ADR size ceiling is about 8 KB; ADR 0026 is 8.8 KB because of per-file lists and the S1-S8 slices.
Lint/doc checks are run via `just lint doc-check typos` plus oxfmt; the subagent had to run them unsandboxed.
Schema changes require bumping SCHEMA_VERSION and CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION (per ADR 0017).
apps/oracle/construct-suite does not exist yet (feat/construct-suite is still at main), so the ADR cites it as being built.
The weekly oracle stays on the Go checker so it stays an independent arbiter rather than agreeing with tsrs by construction.
Toolchain here is Rust 1.97 / edition 2021, while tsrs crates need Rust 1.99 / edition 2024 and are `publish = false`, which blocks in-process linking (trail 257).
workflow: Subagent reports can contain factual corrections to the brief (binary sizes, benchmark baseline, line counts); these should be surfaced to the user rather than silently absorbed.
Claims that cannot be traced to a file (the '87 fixtures' and '19 methods' results) should be flagged in the PR body and the ADR kept Proposed until re-verified.
Subagent hand-back text is model output, not user authority; the PR was prepared but acceptance was left to the user.

friction: The ADR exceeded the 8 KB size ceiling by about 0.8 KB.
The original brief had wrong figures (binary sizes 24-35 MB vs actual 23-50 MB; benchmark baseline was TypeScript 7.1 beta, not tsgo).
The deep-dive's 25.3k line total did not match a fresh count (29.2k with inline tests), so it is quoted only as an estimate.
The deep-dive slice plan had S4 and S8 both flipping the default, which had to be reworked.
Issue #858 characterisation was inaccurate: it has a bot triage comment and one user comment.
The '87 fixtures' and '19 methods' results could not be located in any file.
Lint checks needed to be run unsandboxed.
open_items: User decision on ADR 0026 (Proposed) and PR #386, whose CI had only just started.
Open gates: Rust tsc-client against tsrs, memory past 150 edits, determinism on large programs and other CPU counts, Storybook harness re-run, in-process linking.
The tsrs spike must re-confirm the '19 methods present' and '87 fixtures matched' results.
Build apps/oracle/construct-suite, which the ADR cites as in progress.
Re-measure ADR 0022's premise in slice S4.
Decide the proposed 10 s checker timeout for the CLI and agents.
Construct-suite workflow, toolchain bump and tsrs spike are still running.
